speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to begin my assessment, have you noticed if these symptoms worsen significantly during physical activity or exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The symptom fluctuation (worsening with activity, improving with rest) combined with ocular and limb weakness is characteristic of this autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. I recommend requesting an Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test and a Chest CT to evaluate for thymoma.
